title: One-Step Growth Curves for Cyanophages
author: Matthew Sullivan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.dan2dd
materials: Flash freeze in liquid nitrogen daily.
Lay out the SN bottom agar plates
Keep warm in the 35°C water bath
Plate using 4ml SN top agar per plate.

steps.title: Prepare host culture split
steps.instruction: From an already growing host culture, split the cells at the ratio you will use for the one‑step experiment.

steps.title: Measure host growth daily
steps.instruction: Immediately after the split, take a “time 0” growth reading with a clean 96‑well plate reader. Continue taking readings at approximately the same time each day for 21 days, graph the results and identify the exponential growth phase. Repeat the entire growth‑curve measurement two more times to confirm consistency.

steps.title: Fix exponential‑phase sample
steps.instruction: During the third growth curve, when exponential growth is occurring, fix 1 ml of cells with 5 µl of 25 % glutaraldehyde and store the fixed sample at –80 °C.

steps.title: Determine cell concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the cell count of the exponential‑phase culture (using flow cytometry or DAPI) that corresponds to the fluorescence level measured on the plate reader.

steps.title: Quantify lysate and calculate phage volume
steps.instruction: Perform a plaque assay on the lysate you plan to use to obtain PFU ml⁻¹, then calculate the volume of lysate required to provide 10⁷ phage particles for the infection.

steps.title: Set up media and flask
steps.instruction: Turn on a water bath to 35 °C. Label a 1 L flask with the phage name, host name, and your initials. Add 396 ml of SN media (or enough to bring the total to 400 ml) to the flask.

steps.title: Prepare bottom agar plates
steps.instruction: Days in advance, pour 240 SN bottom‑agar plates (2 ml SN bottom agar per plate).

steps.title: Label tubes and plates
steps.instruction: Label one 15 ml snap‑cap tube as “Infection Tube”. Label 230 additional 15 ml snap‑cap tubes, 230 SN bottom‑agar plates, and 2 plates as “Host (‑)” according to the IDs in Table 1 of the guidelines. Also label 262 × 1.5 µl centrifuge tubes with the same IDs.

steps.title: Add media to labeled tubes
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml of host culture to each of the 15 ml snap‑cap tubes. Add 900 µl SN media to the tubes highlighted in yellow (Table 1) and 990 µl SN media to the tubes highlighted in blue (Table 1). Aliquot heated SN top agar into 50 ml conical tubes for later plating.

steps.title: Calculate and add host and phage
steps.instruction: Determine the culture concentration at the intended infection start using the fluorescence‑cell‑count correlation. Calculate the volume of host culture needed to provide 10⁸ cells (adjust to 2 ml with SN media) and pipet this volume into the “Infection Tube”. Add 10⁷ phage particles (adjust to 2 ml with SN media) to the same tube.

steps.title: Allow phage adsorption
steps.instruction: Incubate the infection mixture for 1 hour (01:00:00) to allow phages to adsorb to the host cells.

steps.title: Dilute infection to 1:100
steps.instruction: Transfer the 4 ml infection mixture into the 396 ml SN media in the 1 L flask, achieving a 1:100 dilution of the infection.

steps.title: Collect time‑0 sample and filter
steps.instruction: Immediately after dilution, take a 1 ml sample (time 0). Remove the plunger of a 1 ml luer‑lock syringe, attach a 0.2 µm, 25 mm diameter syringe filter, draw the 1 ml sample with a serological pipette, replace the plunger and filter the sample into a 1.5 ml centrifuge tube. (Phage concentration should be ≈10⁻⁵ ml⁻¹ at this point.)

steps.title: Perform serial dilutions for free phage
steps.instruction: Serially dilute the filtered sample to a 10⁻³ dilution (≈10² ml⁻¹). Add 250 µl of the 10⁻³ dilution and 250 µl of the 10⁻² dilution to separate 15 ml snap‑cap tubes each containing 1 ml host.

steps.title: Incubate diluted samples with host
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes from the previous step for 2 hours (02:00:00). After incubation, plate each tube using 4 ml SN top agar per plate.

steps.title: Repeat sampling over experiment
steps.instruction: Continue sampling the flask at regular intervals for 16 hours (and once more at 24 hours). For each time point, repeat the steps of sample collection, filtration, serial dilution, host incubation (2 h), and plating.

steps.title: Plate multiple dilutions at later times
steps.instruction: At later time points, plate a range of dilutions (10⁻², 10⁻³, 10⁻⁴, 10⁻⁵) to ensure countable plaque numbers.

steps.title: Count plaques and calculate PFU
steps.instruction: After 7 days incubation, count plaques on all plates with countable numbers. Calculate PFU ml⁻¹ for each time point for both centrifuged (free phage) and un‑centrifuged (total phage) samples and graph the results.

steps.title: Compute burst size
steps.instruction: Determine the average free‑phage PFU on the plateau before the burst (A) and after the burst (B). Subtract A from B to obtain C (total new phages released). Divide C by the number of infecting phages (total phage at T0 minus free phage at T0) to obtain the burst size.
